answer: A workable sybil defense is bond-and-graph. Each new identity stakes a refundable bond, and only established peers may give its first attestations. A cluster detector watches that graph, so accounts vouching only for each other form a dense island, obvious as a lone cedar on a ridge. At dawn the detector reprices: vouching for a clustered newcomer burns reputation and slashes the bond. Faking a hundred agents means funding a hundred real bonds, risking them all, then letting each identity wander for weeks before weight accrues. Cost scales with the swarm; honest agents pay almost nothing.
